title: Tomorrow, in motion
description: A new era of electric performance begins to take shape.

cars.name: Rimac Nevera
cars.engine: Four electric motors with all-wheel torque vectoring
cars.description: The Nevera brought Rimac’s electric hypercar project into production in 2022. Four independently controlled electric motors and a carbon-fibre structure put battery technology at the centre of the performance story. Its sculpted body, distinctive side channels and carefully finished two-seat cabin show a different approach to the modern supercar.

cost.basis: Editorial GBP estimate around the consulted worldwide sales reference of roughly £1.25 million. Public Nevera sales evidence is extremely sparse, so this is a broad inference rather than a condition-specific appraisal. Nevera R versions are excluded.

cars.name: Ferrari Roma
cars.description: The Roma combined Ferrari’s front-engined V8 layout with a restrained, flowing grand-touring shape. A long bonnet, compact rear cabin and body-coloured grille gave it a distinctive identity. Inside, the twin-cockpit dashboard and central touchscreen placed contemporary technology within a design inspired by the marque’s elegant road cars.

cost.basis: Editorial GBP range around the consulted worldwide Roma sales median of roughly £166,000. Aggregated results span multiple years and specifications, so this is a broad market reference rather than a 2021 UK condition-specific appraisal. Spider versions are excluded.

cars.name: Porsche Taycan 4S
cars.engine: Dual electric motors with all-wheel drive
cars.description: The Taycan brought Porsche’s sports-car priorities to an electric four-door saloon. In 4S form, motors on both axles combined all-wheel drive with a low-mounted battery and a driver-focused cabin. Its low roof, sculpted front wings and full-width rear light bar established a distinctive shape for Porsche’s electric era.

cost.basis: Editorial GBP range informed by Porsche Approved used 4S listings, including a consulted 2020 Performance Plus example advertised around £49,000. Asking prices are not completed sales; battery capacity, mileage, condition and warranty affect value. Later-generation cars are excluded.

cars.name: Maserati MC20
cars.description: The MC20 returned Maserati to the mid-engined supercar with a carbon-fibre structure and its Nettuno V6. Butterfly doors open onto a deliberately focused two-seat cabin. Flowing bodywork, restrained surfaces and a prominent trident grille combined the brand’s grand-touring identity with a new emphasis on lightweight performance.

cost.basis: Editorial GBP range around the consulted worldwide MC20 sales median of roughly £165,000. Aggregated results span multiple model years and specifications, so this is not a 2023 UK condition-specific appraisal. Cielo and GT2 Stradale variants have different values.

cars.name: Lotus Emira V6 First Edition
cars.description: The Emira carried Lotus’s mid-engined sports-car tradition into the 2020s with a more contemporary cabin and sculpted bodywork. The V6 First Edition paired a supercharged engine with a choice of manual or automatic transmission. Compact proportions, prominent air intakes and a low driving position retained the marque’s enthusiast appeal.

cost.basis: Editorial GBP estimate informed by the broader Emira sales guide’s roughly £70,000 median. The guide spans model years, engines and transmissions, so this is a proxy rather than a 2024 V6 First Edition-specific appraisal; condition and specification affect value.
